title: Auth-class declaration: every endpoint names its class and middleware enforces it
asA: security reviewer auditing the API surface
iWant: each endpoint's auth posture declared in the contract and enforced by middleware, not by handler code
soThat: the auth posture of the whole surface is enumerable from the spec and cannot be silently weakened

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every operation in the generated OpenAPI spec carries the x-auth-class extension with one of exactly four values: public, user, admin, or service.
acceptanceCriteria.when: every operation's x-auth-class value is read
acceptanceCriteria.then: each carries exactly one of the four declared values and no other

acceptanceCriteria.description: An endpoint without a declared auth class fails contract validation at build time; classlessness is a build failure, not a default.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a deliberately added endpoint with no auth-class declaration
acceptanceCriteria.then: validation fails naming the classless endpoint

acceptanceCriteria.description: Class enforcement happens in middleware before the handler runs; a handler is never invoked for a request that fails its endpoint's class check.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a request failing the endpoint's auth-class check
acceptanceCriteria.then: the middleware rejects it and the handler observably does not execute

acceptanceCriteria.description: Enforcement is driven by the same declaration the spec publishes: changing an endpoint's declared class changes its enforcement with no second edit site.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an endpoint whose declared class is changed from user to admin
acceptanceCriteria.when: the service is rebuilt and the endpoint called with a non-admin user token
acceptanceCriteria.then: the request is rejected per the new class, and the spec and enforcement agree

acceptanceCriteria.description: Auth rejections use the declared error envelope with correct status semantics: 401 for missing or invalid credentials, 403 for valid credentials lacking the required class.
acceptanceCriteria.given: requests with absent, invalid, and under-privileged credentials
acceptanceCriteria.when: each is submitted to a protected endpoint
acceptanceCriteria.then: responses are 401, 401, and 403 respectively, each with a problem-details body

acceptanceCriteria.description: The four middleware classes are the only auth paths in the service; no endpoint implements bespoke auth logic outside its class middleware.
acceptanceCriteria.when: auth logic outside the four class middlewares is searched for
acceptanceCriteria.then: none exists; every endpoint's auth behaviour is fully attributable to its declared class
